intent: I want artificial turf for my dog on the Grand Strand, anywhere from Shallotte, NC to Burgess, SC. What do I need to plan for here that a generic pet-turf page won't tell me: summer heat and shade rules, what counts as shelter, how far a tie-out has to reach, where waste and rinse water may go, flood-zone permits, and anything special if I keep several dogs?
distinctValue: The national pet-turf page covers layout, cleaning access and odor in general terms, and sibling Grand Strand pages already carry the Leon/Newhan soil pair and the state-line pervious-surface rules, so this page carries neither. It is built on the local animal, stormwater and flood codes that change how a dog area is laid out, each read in the live Municode text through the Municode API on 2026-09-12, with the code version dated. (1) Heat and shelter: NOAA 1991-2020 monthly normals for the North Myrtle Beach airport (July 87.6 F, August 86.5 F). Horry County Sec. 4-3(b)(1)c requires whole-body shade in daylight at a forecast or actual 85 F for a dog outside more than thirty minutes without an owner or caretaker present, says a doghouse is inadequate protection from the sun, and 4-3(b)(1)e says trees and shrubbery do not meet the criteria for proper shelter; Sec. 4-2 keeps the chapter out of incorporated municipalities unless they opt in. North Myrtle Beach Sec. 4-1 requires whole-body shade for dogs outside and unattended with no temperature trigger, expressly including a fenced yard, and Sec. 4-5(e) bars leaving such a dog out in a National Weather Service severe weather advisory or warning. Brunswick County, NC Sec. 1-3-101 defines adequate shelter as an enclosure of at least three sides, a roof and a floor and excludes space underneath outside steps, decks and stoops. (2) Tie-outs, found on no other page: Horry 4-3(d)(2) (tether at least eight feet with swivels at both ends; trolley no less than eight feet long and no more than seven feet above ground; nothing that impedes the tether; no tethering above 90 F or in thunderstorms, tropical storms or hurricanes), tied to NOAA's annual normal of 20.9 days a year at or above 90 F at the same station; North Myrtle Beach 4-5(d) (at least ten feet or four times body length, not across the property line, not 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. or with no owner or keeper present); Myrtle Beach 4-1 and Conway 6-4-21 (tethering more than two hours in any continuous twelve-hour period, or with no responsible person present, is mistreatment); Brunswick County 1-3-103(13) (at least ten feet of travel perpendicular to the anchor; a pulley's stationary cable at least ten feet) and 1-3-254 (an animal housed or restrained less than fifteen feet from a public street, road or sidewalk may be deemed a public nuisance at Animal Protective Services' discretion). (3) Water and waste: the drainage and waste-free containment clause shared by Horry 4-3 and NMB 4-1; Horry 10-19 (mosquito breeding; keep ditches, ponds and pipes clear); NMB 13-85(a) (no pet fecal matter left on public or private property where it may cause or contribute to pollution); Conway 6-4-36(c) (animal waste disposed of without harm to the environment); Brunswick 1-3-103(2) (shelter and surrounding area kept clean at all times); Horry 17.7-29(b)(1) exceptions list lawn watering and landscape irrigation but not washing a pet area, so the page says ask the county. (4) Flood-zone lots: Horry Ch. 9 Sec. 9-1 (development includes filling, grading and excavation; supplemental flood zone; compensatory storage), 9-5 (scope), 9-6 (permit before development), 9-33 (apply to the floodplain administrator), 9-51(13) (compensatory storage when fill is used); the page says to ask whether extra base counts as fill and does not assert that it does. Myrtle Beach 4-1 and Conway 6-4-21 treat failing to provide shelter from floods, tropical storms or hurricanes as mistreatment. (5) Several dogs: Myrtle Beach 4-1 kennel definition (an owner or keeper of four or more dogs over four months of age) and 4-12 (inspection; non-commercial kennels on the sanitary sewer with sealed impervious floors sloped half an inch per foot; 15 square feet per animal). (6) North Carolina side: Brunswick County Ch. 1-3 as codified on Municode (Supplement 26, codified through Ordinance No. UDO-21-01 of May 17, 2021; the tethering subsection was last amended 3-19-18); Municode's OrdBank lists three Ordinances of 10-20-2025 awaiting codification whose text the API did not return, so the page tells readers to ask the sheriff's Animal Protective Services whether the rules have changed and whether they reach a town address. Shallotte Ch. 91 (Republication, tracked through 2026-04-30) holds only barking-dog nuisance, running at large, and abatement and penalty sections. Carolina Shores' code is on American Legal, which returned 403 on 2026-09-12, so the page makes no claim about it and says ask the town. The page no longer names or states N.C.G.S. 143-214.7D (ncleg.gov HTML and PDF returned 403 on 2026-09-12) and no longer carries the NMB pervious-surface FAQ, the Myrtle Beach odor and stormwater feces rules, the USDA soil sentence or a process recap. No claim rests on the Horry County, Myrtle Beach or SC DES websites.

Sec. 4-2. - Applicability. The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to those areas of the county located within the confines of any legally incorporated municipality within the county, unless a majority of the governing body of a municipality, by written and signed resolution, formally requests to include the area of such municipality within the coverage of this chapter and the county council has acted favorably on such a request and has so notified such municipality of its approval of such a request. (Ord. No. 69-07, 5-15-07)

Sec. 4-3(b)(1): The containment area for the animal shall be free of accumulated waste and debris so that the animal shall be free to walk or lie down without coming in contact with waste or debris; shall be free of unsanitary conditions; reasonable measures should be taken to keep the area free of ticks, fleas, flies, and also comply with the county mosquito ordinance section 10-19, exterior property maintenance. A suitable method of drainage shall be provided to rapidly eliminate any excess water or moisture.
For dogs outside for more than thirty (30) minutes without the physical presence of an owner or caretaker, proper shelter shall meet the following minimum standards:

c. During times when the forecasted or actual outdoor temperature measures eighty-five (85) degrees Fahrenheit or higher, each dog must be afforded one (1) or more separate areas of shade large enough to accommodate the entire body of the dog at one time to ensure protection from the direct rays of the sun during all daylight hours. A doghouse is inadequate protection from the sun.
e. Trees, shrubbery, abandoned cars and the like, stacked cages without dividers, cages with wire floors without a solid resting platform, do not meet the criteria for "proper shelter"

Sec. 4-3(d)(2) Tethering. It shall be unlawful to tether an animal while outdoors except when all of the following conditions are met: a. The animal must be over the age of six (6) months. ... c. The tether has the following properties: 1. A minimum eight-foot length; 2. A swivel-type termination at both ends; and 3. Total weight does not exceed ten (10) percent of the animal's body weight. d. The animal is not tethered outside during extreme weather, including, but not limited to, temperatures above ninety (90) degrees Fahrenheit or below forty-five (45) degrees Fahrenheit snow hail tornadoes, thunderstorms tropical storms or hurricanes. e. The animal is tethered so as to prevent injury, strangulation or entanglement. f. The animal has access to water and shelter. g. The animal is not tethered where any object may interfere or impede free movement of the tether. ... k. Any pulley, running line or trolley system to which a tether is attached shall be no less than eight (8) feet in length and no more than seven (7) feet above ground.

sources.label: North Myrtle Beach Code of Ordinances, Ch. 4, Art. I, Sec. 4-1 (Definitions)
supports: Municode latest job for product 11359 (API, read 2026-09-12): Supplement 106, codified through Ordinance No. 26-12, adopted March 16, 2026; MaxTrackingDate 2026-07-23 (current through 23 July 2026).

Adequate shelter: That shelter which will keep a non-aquatic animal dry, out of the direct path of winds and out of the direct sun and at a temperature level that is healthful for the animal. The containment area for the animal shall be free of accumulated waste and debris so that the animal shall be free to walk or lie down without coming in contact with waste or debris. A suitable method of drainage shall be provided to rapidly eliminate any excess water or moisture.

For dogs left outside and unattended, adequate shelter shall meet the following minimum standards: ... (c) All dogs must be afforded one (1) or more separate areas of shade large enough to accommodate the entire body of the dog at one (1) time to ensure protection from the direct rays of the sun.

Outside and unattended: Any dog who is exposed to the elements for a duration of longer than fifteen (15) minutes and not in visual range and physical presence of the owner. This expressly includes, but is not limited to, a dog in a securely fenced-in yard, a dog in a kennel, or a dog that is tethered.
Extreme weather: Any period in which a severe weather advisory or warning has been issued for the area by the National Weather Service.

sources.label: North Myrtle Beach Code of Ordinances, Ch. 4, Art. I, Sec. 4-5 (Cruelty to or poisoning of animals)
supports: (d) It shall be unlawful for any person to allow a dog to be tethered: (1) between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. or when no owner or keeper of the dog is present on the premises; (2) by a tether of less than ten (10) feet in length, or less than four (4) times the length of the dog's body from tip of nose to base of tail, whichever is greater; (3) by a tether the length of which allows the dog to cross the property line of the property on which it is tethered; (4) using a logging chain, tow chain, or other tether that causes injury or pain to the dog because of the material of which it is made or because of the size or weight of the tether; (5) by attaching the tether to the dog by a collar that is not properly fitted or by means of a choke chain collar, pinch collar, or prong collar; (6) in an area likely to cause injury or pain to the dog because of entanglement or because of surrounding structures.
(e) It shall be unlawful to leave a dog outside and unattended during extreme weather. (Code 1970, §§ 5-5, 5-6; Ord. of 3-19-80; Ord. No. 02-45, § 2, 10-21-02; Ord. No. 19-36, 8-19-19)

Sec. 4-1: Kennel means any facility wherein a person, business entity or organization regularly keeps six or more dogs or other animals for any purpose and receives compensation or barter for the service or for the sale of the animal, or a owner or keeper of four or more dogs over four months of age.

Sec. 4-1: Mistreatment of animals means a failure, whether intentional or not, to provide veterinary care or wholesome and adequate food, water and appropriate shelter, kept free of waste and debris and which provides protection from harsh weather including, but not limited to, extreme heat, freezing temperatures, snow, hail, tornadoes, thunderstorms, floods, tropical storms or hurricanes. ... Mistreatment shall also include tethering of an animal for more than two hours in any continuous twelve-hour period, tethering of an animal on a premise without a responsible person present, tethering of an animal that is sick or injured, tethering of an animal on a restraining device that exceeds more than ten percent of the body weight of the animal and has a length of less than ten feet, tethering of an animal by any chain or metal restraining devise in which the metal is in direct contact with the skin, and tethering of an animal in such a manner as to cause injury, strangulation or entanglement.

Sec. 4-12. - Kennels. No person shall own or operate a kennel without an inspection by the animal control officer. Commercial kennels shall be constructed, maintained and operated in conformance with the current standards and procedures promulgated by the Humane Society of the United States. Non-commercial kennels must be connected to the city's sanitary sewer system with floors constructed of impervious material, treated with sealer and a slope of at least one half inch per foot for drainage to the sanitary sewer. Enclosures must have at least 15 square feet per animal and comply with all applicable building and zoning codes for structures. (Ord. No. 2001-17, 7-10-01)

Adequate shelter means an enclosure of at least three (3) sides, a roof and a floor. The enclosure shall be ventilated and must have sufficient room for the animal(s) to move around freely and to lie down comfortably. Animals housed under the following conditions shall not constitute adequate shelter: (1) Underneath outside steps, decks and stoops; (2) Inside of vehicles; (3) Underneath vehicles; (4) Inside metal barrels placed in direct sunlight during the summer; or (5) Inside cardboard boxes.

Sec. 1-3-3(1): Authority is hereby granted to the county sheriff to enforce this chapter. This chapter shall be enforced by the sheriff, all sheriff's deputies, and all animal protective services officers.

supports: (2) Clean shelter. All shelter for animals and the area surrounding said shelter shall be kept clean at all times.

(13) Tethering. Tethering is defined as a means of tying or fastening a dog outdoors on a rope, cable, or other line for the purpose of restraint. Tethering does not include restraint of a dog on an attended leash. Tethering is prohibited except as set out hereafter. Dogs over six (6) months of age may be tethered to a restraint system outdoors. A restraint system can be an overhead pulley system, a retractable cable system or a swiveled cable anchored into the ground. All of these systems must allow the dog a minimum of ten (10) feet of travel perpendicular to the anchor point. For a pulley system, the stationary cable that the pulley runs on must be at least ten (10) feet in length and anchored on each end to a stationary object. The line attached to the pulley must allow the dog to move perpendicularly at least ten (10) feet from the stationary cable. ... (Ord. of 6-18-12; Ord. of 3-19-18, § 1)

supports: Sec. 9-1: Development means any man-made change to improved or unimproved real estate, including, but not limited to, buildings or other structures, dredging, filling, grading, paving, excavation or drilling operations, or storage of equipment or materials.

Sec. 9-1: Supplemental flood zone means an official map created to approximate the actual extent of the flooding post Hurricane Florence and which created subzones to adjust for elevation differences in the flood.

Sec. 9-1: Compensatory storage means offset of any loss of flood storage capacity. The developer is required to offset new fill (dirt or compacted soil) put in the floodplain or supplemental flood zone by excavating an additional floodable area to replace the lost flood storage area. This should be done at a hydraulically equivalent sites. Engineering analyses must be provided to determine the adequacy of off-setting compensatory excavation.

Sec. 9-5: This chapter shall apply to all areas of special flood hazard within the jurisdiction of the county as identified by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) in its flood insurance study, dated December 16, 2021 with accompanying maps and other supporting data that are hereby adopted by reference and declared to be a part of this chapter. ... This chapter also applies to any areas identified on the supplemental flood zone maps as shown in attachment A to the ordinance from which this chapter derived entitled "supplemental flood zone." With the exception of roads within the supplemental flood zones.

Sec. 9-6. - Establishment of development permit. A development permit shall be required in conformance with the provisions of this chapter prior to the commencement of any development activities. (Ord. No. 68-2021, § 1, 7-13-21)
